answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them at the bottom; shuffle nine Conflict II cards and deal five above them; shuffle three Conflict I cards and deal one on top. The resulting deck has 1 I, 5 II, and 4 III; return unused cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 2: ‘Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In a four-player game a human starts at 1 VP; in a three-player game at 0 VP. In either game the human starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, three troops in their garrison and nine in supply, and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: score 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents and Swordmaster; three troops in garrison, nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, and after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Only the Reveal boxes of cards revealed for that Reveal turn supply Reveal effects; Agent-turn cards’ Reveal boxes are ignored. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Agent turns are optional’; after Reveal, turns are skipped; Reveal effects use just-revealed cards; Clean Up moves all cards in front of you to discard.

answers.answer: No: the played card’s and destination’s effects happen after the entry cost, so they cannot pay that same cost; a legal Plot Intrigue played before placing the Agent can grant resources that are available to pay it. One card sends only one Agent using one matching icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn and may only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Plot gains before entry can pay; card and destination gains after placement cannot; Agent Turn says one icon and one Agent; cards with no Agent icons only on Reveal.

answers.answer: At a Combat space all three troops recruited that turn can deploy, plus up to two more from the garrison: at most five here. At a non-Combat space recruited troops go to the garrison and cannot deploy there. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: deploy any/all units recruited during the current turn plus up to two from garrison; troop recruitment takes it from supply to garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to a post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy at a connected post to enter a space occupied by another player; it does not bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card, and must be chosen just after placing the Agent, before space/card effects. You cannot use the same Spy for both; you may use two separate Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence effects; Gather timing; same Spy cannot pay both, but Research Station example permits two Spies.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops give 4, one sandworm gives 3, and four revealed swords give 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you are ineligible to play Combat Intrigue, which is available only to players with at least one unit there.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop = 2, sandworm = 3, sword = 1; last unit removed means 0. Combat phase: players with at least one unit may play Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes, passing does not prevent you acting again if an opponent plays afterward. The window closes once all involved players pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; closes after consecutive passes; cleanup returns troops, resets markers, returns worms to bank.

answers.answer: When two players tie for first in either game, each receives the second reward, nobody wins the Conflict, and nobody takes its card; in a four-player game the remaining players compete for the third reward if exactly two tied for first. A player at 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first each gain second reward and no one wins or takes card; in 4 players with exactly two tied, remaining compete for third. Resolve Combat: 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double your reward once; having two does not quadruple it. Control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For an optional cost reward such as 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay the cost a second time to receive it a second time (3 spice for 1 VP twice, or 6 for 2 VP).
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more’; control and battle icons excluded; optional cost may be paid a second time, with 3 spice/1 VP example.

answers.answer: After winning and taking a Conflict card face up, check for a matching icon against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A match is mandatory: flip the matching pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame the wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: after you win and take card, check another face-up Conflict or Objective; ‘must’ flip pair; Endgame wild match.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP and lose that VP below 2; reaching 2 again earns it again. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if Influence falls below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first to 4 also gains the Alliance token and its 1 VP; tying the current holder does not steal it, an opponent must rise higher. Alliance VP transfers with the token and the prior holder loses it.
answers.evidence: Victory Points, Faction Influence: 2 VP reversal; separate 4 track bonus and Alliance VP; tie does not steal, rise higher transfers.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent during the Reveal turn before, between, or after Reveal effects. It can be pooled from multiple sources for one card or split from one source across cards. The Imperium Row replenishes immediately, so you may buy a replacement if able. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Persuasion timing, pool/split, Row always five and replacement may be acquired, acquired card enters face-up discard.

answers.answer: At Makers, each Maker space without an Agent gains 1 spice in its bonus spot, accumulating across rounds; visiting gains all bonus spice there. Deep Desert and Hagga Basin offer base spice or sandworms if you have Maker Hooks (Deep Desert: 4 spice or two worms; Hagga: 2 spice or one worm). Hooks are not spent, and a summoning effect that does not specify Hooks does not require them. No worm can be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while Shield Wall remains; after it is removed any Conflict may receive a worm. Worms can never enter a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers and Sandworms: bonus spice accumulates; Deep Desert/Hagga options; Hooks not universal prerequisite or spent; Shield Wall protects named locations; worms never garrisoned.

answers.answer: At Recall at the end of a round, 10+ VP by any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then most VP wins. The stated resource tiebreakers, in order, are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory: end at end of round; Endgame Intrigue then compare VP; tiebreakers listed in order.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup has 2 contracts face up under the Landsraad Council and 18 face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue and four Imperium cards. Shaddam is an optional Leader choice, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and stay in the box; they do not replace the 20 standard contracts.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes: 20 contracts, flip two and remaining 18 face down; shuffle four each additional card type; Shaddam option. Components note contrasting backs only Rise of Ix.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it from the bank face up; when none remain, it gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining its shown spice amount in total that turn; Immediate completes upon taking it; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Taking contracts and Completing contracts paragraphs specify icon fallback and each contract completion trigger.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a board space after already sending your Agent there this turn, completion must wait until a future turn; you must hold the contract at the time you send the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: contract taken after visit waits for future turn; announce, gain rewards, flip face down, leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It receives the Ornithopter Objective; humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives. First Player is the human whose Objective shows the marker, and alternates only between humans. Order is First Player, Rival, other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules, Setup and Agent turns: one shared Rival; Ornithopter Objective; human First Player; order; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: For an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try the specified empty post, ignore placement if none, and immediately reveal another card either way. Ignore ordinary space costs and effects; apply only printed Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: occupied destination ignored; Place Spy and empty deck/Reshuffle behavior; ignore normal costs/effects.

answers.answer: For 3–4 players, remove Objectives whose 1-3P/4/6P marking does not match the player count, then each player draws one at random. The Objective showing the First Player marker chooses the first player. Shaddam may not be used without CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5: Shaddam only with CHOAM; match player-count markings, draw one randomly, marker identifies First Player.

answers.answer: Solari, spice, water, and sandworms are not limited: make any convenient substitution if the bank runs out. Troops are limited by your personal supply; if it is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return there. Resource gains come from the bank and payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: resources/sandworms not limited; take gains from bank and return payments. Recruiting: empty troop supply means no recruiting until return.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal the top Conflict card and then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases and Phase 1/5 descriptions; Player Reference repeats the five phases.

answers.answer: Yes, board-space, Agent-box, and Faction Influence effects may be carried out in any order. No, entry requirements and costs are checked and paid immediately before effects, so the Influence gained from that visit cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: costs/requirements before resolving effects; then space/card effects and Faction advance may be in any order.

answers.answer: Normally an arrow cost/effect may be used only once per turn, even if you can pay twice; sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward is the exception. Most card and space effects are mandatory. “May,” optional arrow costs, and black-X trash are optional; direct instruction to trash itself is mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs: once per turn except doubled Conflict rewards. FAQ mandatory effects and costs lists exceptions and Intrigue requirement.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one from a post for no effect. If a placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type, only a post meeting that condition is legal; otherwise you cannot place the Spy.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: unoccupied post; recall one if none in supply; specified Agent icon must be connected to post.

answers.answer: No: Infiltrate only bypasses another player’s Agent, not your own. A Spy recall still requires playing a card for the Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you may use one Spy for Infiltrate and another for Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts and FAQ Spies: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; recall requires card; two different effects allowed but not two Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The controller gets the separate visit bonus whenever anyone, including the controller, visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning the corresponding Conflict transfers control by placing your marker over the former controller’s; on revealing a Conflict for a space you already control, you may deploy one troop from supply to the Conflict, without a visit.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: visitor-triggered controller bonus; winning conflict replaces marker; defensive bonus from supply on Conflict reveal.

answers.answer: In a tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps their rewards and card, and no further rewards are given. A tie for third gets nothing. If three or more tie for first in a four-player game, all tied get second reward and no one wins/takes the card; no other rewards are given.
answers.evidence: Combat ties rules in Special Rules & Edge Cases.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second receive their ordinary rewards and third receives none. This remains true in two-player play when the Rival participates: the Rival counts as the third competitor, and ordinary third place gets no reward.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: in 2 or 3 players ordinary first and second rewards; third gets nothing except tie for second; two humans plus Rival is included.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigue may be played during your Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigue only during Combat; Endgame Intrigue only at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down separately from your deck; after resolving one, place it face up in its discard pile. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section and FAQ Draw timing: type timings, separate face-down holding, face-up discard, reshuffle discard when deck empty.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand, and cannot be an Intrigue unless the effect specifies it. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon lets you trash one Intrigue of your choice from hand. Secrets takes one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding and Trashing sections; Secrets board-space row and Intrigue cards section specify random theft at 4+.

answers.answer: Trash effects can remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card instructs you to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its already acquired VP.
answers.evidence: Trashing paragraph; FAQ Victory says The Spice Must Flow acquire VP is retained if trashed.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once at the moment of acquisition. If your deck is empty when drawing, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Persuasion cannot be saved: unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards; Persuasion can never be saved and discard reshuffle when deck empty.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn remain in play through Clean Up. A Fremen Bond card works if you have one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order. They cease being in play when moved to discard at Clean Up, unless trashed first.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond paragraph.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just sent; the returned Agent may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to garrison. “Retreat any number” includes zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ Combat and troops states retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: A single free-choice effect granting two Influence must place both with one chosen Faction; it cannot be split. An Alliance icon requires you to hold that Faction’s Alliance token, and a minimum-Influence effect requires meeting its stated Influence threshold.
answers.evidence: Influence: free choice gaining two cannot choose two Factions; Alliance icon requires holding token; card effects may require minimum Influence.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if several were tied, the former holder chooses which receives it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more to take it, return it to the board. Losing it also loses its VP.
answers.evidence: FAQ Alliance loss paragraph.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards then drawn. A Plot Intrigue whose effect applies at Reveal stays face up until then, is used, and is then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing paragraph.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first, because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops paragraph.

answers.answer: If VP and all four listed resources remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory paragraph.

answers.answer: No; fulfill all held contracts for the same space with one Agent placement. Contract effects are another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with space and Agent-box effects. You must have held each contract when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion paragraph.

answers.answer: No, Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts. Sardaukar Commander permits him to choose one of those contracts instead of a generally available one when acquiring a contract. Emperor of the Known Universe takes effect immediately when playing Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam paragraph.

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts on the leftmost Training track space and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica side begins face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications and FAQ final paragraph.

answers.answer: For Margot/Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2 and counts; reaching 2 can trigger again later after losing Influence and moving up to 2 again. Moving down through 2 does not count as reaching it. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: passing 2 counts, regain from below counts, only moving up; Spacing Guild’s Favor clarification.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, has no cost, and draws a card; with CHOAM take a contract, otherwise gain 2 Solari. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, has no cost, gives 1 Emperor Influence, and takes a contract with CHOAM or 2 Solari without it. Accept Contract gives no automatic Influence; Dutiful Service explicitly gives Emperor Influence (not an additional automatic Faction advance beyond that stated effect).
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows; header clarifies Landsraad/City/Spice Trade are not Factions and only listed Influence applies; Faction advance is once total.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, cost 2 water, Combat; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Each also grants all accumulated bonus spice regardless of choosing worms. Hooks are retained, not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows and Sandworm Reward/Sandworms rules: Maker space grants all bonus; Hooks are not spent.

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and at least 2 Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one takes Maker Hooks if lacking them, recruits one troop, and gains 1 water. Option two gains 1 water and may remove the Shield Wall; it does not recruit a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr row.

answers.answer: High Council is Landsraad, costs 5 Solari per visit, and is not a Combat space. First visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gives 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains it and 6 Solari once anyone has one. Each player may visit only once per game. Take the third Agent from beside the board to your Leader; it is available this round and thereafter. A Rival getting Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row, including Rival note.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege is Landsraad; it costs 3 Solari and requires 2+ Emperor Influence. You may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege row; it is Landsraad, not a Faction space.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, costs 3 spice and requires 2+ Guild Influence. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad and not Combat: choose 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops, and paying 2 also gains 1 water. Spice Refinery is City and Combat: choose 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari for free or 4 Solari after paying 1 spice; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner is Spacing Guild, costs 5 spice, gives 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops; it is Combat. Desert Tactics is Fremen, costs 1 water, gives 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop and optionally trashes a card; it is Combat. Sardaukar is Emperor, costs 4 spice, gives 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue and recruits four troops; it is not marked Combat. Thus only Heighliner and Desert Tactics allow normal deployment.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows identify costs/effects and Combat labels.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad, no cost; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild, no cost; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear’s red box is ignored during Reveal, or when the card gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ final paragraph: False Orders and Litany Against Fear clarifications.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it remains unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate clarification.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes on the bottoms of Influence tracks, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. Its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and the Rival can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup; Rival is a scoring competitor and 10+ VP triggers Endgame.

answers.answer: As soon as its Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water total reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends that many resources and takes its third Agent for use in the current round. Each resource/card counts as one. It spends Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, then water; leftovers remain.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster paragraph.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, the Rival spends each qualifying set for 1 VP: 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water. A mixed total of seven is not a qualifying set and cannot be spent for VP.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources: whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival uses the Faction with least Influence and breaks ties by leftmost priority. It gains Influence VP at 2 and Alliance VP when holding a token, but does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: least Influence and leftmost tie-break; Rival rules: gains/loses Influence VP and Alliances but no 4-Influence resource bonus; numbered icon explanation.

answers.answer: No. On a two-destination card, use only the destination selected by its current condition (Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping; Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner); if occupied, reveal another card rather than use the other destination.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns, two-destination card rules.

answers.answer: At every Combat space, the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. At a noncombat space newly recruited troops go to garrison, not Conflict. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus that it does not qualify for is ignored; lack of the bonus never prevents placing the Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons and Combat deployment; conditional 2+ bonus never prevents placement.

answers.answer: Unless a type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in its priority order; if all four are occupied it ignores placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes paragraph.

answers.answer: If its Scheme recruits troops before Agent placement and it then visits a Combat space that turn, deploy those troops too. A Place Spy card with no legal post is ignored, but the Rival still immediately reveals another Hagal card and continues the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Place Spy rules in Rival Agent turns.

answers.answer: With Hooks, Hagga Basin/Deep Desert summon one/two worms respectively instead of taking base spice, if the Conflict permits worms. Without Hooks, take base spice (2/4); a protected Conflict blocks worms while Shield Wall remains, so take base spice instead. In every case collect all accumulated bonus spice at the visited Maker space.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: always collects bonus; worm/base spice choice, Hook and protected Conflict conditions.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords as strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph.

answers.answer: Yes: the Rival gains control bonuses, defensive troops from supply, battle-icon VP and normal rewards; one or more sandworms doubles rewards. It always takes optional Conflict VP when it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts, and a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat paragraph.

answers.answer: During Resolve Reveal Effects, total Combat strength and announce it; set the Combat marker at any point while resolving, and update it as needed. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn and Strength sections.

answers.answer: A Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not when you merely reveal it. Card text can override the usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader ability note; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It does not by itself mean Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate recall options without a card.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon; separate Spy recall effects.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot select Intrigue unless specified; discard does not trash it.
answers.evidence: Trashing: separate trash-an-Intrigue icon; Discarding: from hand, not Intrigue unless specified.

answers.answer: Yes. Doubling a reward that grants one Influence of your choice lets you choose the same or different Factions for the two gains. By contrast, one effect explicitly granting two free-choice Influence must assign both to the same Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm doubling example permits same or two different Factions; Influence rule says one gain-two effect cannot choose two Factions.

answers.answer: The Rival resolves its own printed Signet Ring ability from its selected Rival card when Hagal shows the Signet Ring effect. It needs neither a human Signet Ring card nor a Reveal turn; the Rival follows its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities on Agent turns.
answers.evidence: Rival setup says follow its printed Signet Ring and Scheme; Rival takes Agent turns and never Reveals.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon takes a token from the bank if the Rival lacks one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no second token. Shield Wall removal succeeds only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks or after the Wall is already gone, ignore it.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, costs nothing, and is not a Combat space. It grants 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; additionally, each opponent with four or more Intrigues gives the Rival/visitor one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row; Intrigue cards states theft random from each opponent at 4+.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, costs nothing, and is Combat. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice. Its controller separately gains 1 spice, including when the visitor is also the controller.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin row; header says resolve visitor effects and controller bonus even for same player.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict from the top of the deck and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards remaining from earlier rounds. Each player draws five cards after the Conflict reveal and defensive troop bonus.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 Round Start specifies order and location.

answers.answer: Each human’s four Influence cubes start on the bottom spaces of their respective Faction tracks; the four Alliance tokens start on the marked spaces of those tracks. No human starts with an Alliance. The Shield Wall token is placed in its marked board area below Spice Refinery and is initially present.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6; normal setup assigns Maker Hooks to no human, while Alliance tokens are on tracks.

answers.answer: In standard 3–4 player play, the First Player takes the first turn and play proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. Players who Reveal are skipped for the rest of the phase; Player Turns end when all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority starts with First Player and continues clockwise; each eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass. The window closes after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 Player Turns and Phase 3 Combat Intrigue rules.

answers.answer: Reveal turn steps are: Reveal Cards (reveal remaining hand); Resolve Reveal Effects (use the just-revealed cards’ Reveal boxes, acquire with Persuasion, total/announce strength); Clean Up (move all cards in front of you to discard). Reveal effects may be resolved in any order, not necessarily card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn lists three steps and says Reveal box effects may be gained in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s 10-card starting deck face down in their supply. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked Intrigue and Imperium cards before shuffling; keep those decks face down, deal five Imperium cards face up as the Row, and place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Each human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor and Control markers start in that player’s supply (the cubes for Influence are placed on track bottoms).
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4, 6 and Initial card states table.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, ordinary Persuasion acquires any of the five Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way, or The Spice Must Flow from Reserve. Cost is shown at the card’s top right. These purchases use Persuasion during Reveal, not Agent turns.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards paragraph.

answers.answer: Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional, so you may decline even when a legal move exists. Shield Wall detonation/removal is also optional. Once removed, the Wall is returned to the box and cannot return later in the game.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts says ordinary placement and recall optional; Shield Wall says may remove and cannot return.

answers.answer: The played card must have an Agent icon matching the destination. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a City-only card send an Agent there. A card with the Spy Agent icon can access any space connected to a post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn matching icon rule and Spy Agent icon rule.

answers.answer: Yes. During your Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before placement are available to pay entry. Resources from the card played to send the Agent or from the destination occur after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure Plot Intrigue timing and entry cost paragraph.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, skip humans who have Revealed but continue the Rival’s Agent turns while it has an Agent in supply. Combat begins only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Phase 2 two-player Player Turns rule.

answers.answer: Standard board-space access and Combat status: Accept Contract—Spice Trade, no; Arrakeen—City, yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad, no; Deep Desert—Spice Trade, yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild, no; Desert Tactics—Fremen, yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor, no; Espionage—Bene Gesserit, no; Fremkit—Fremen, yes; Gather Support—Landsraad, no; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild, yes; High Council—Landsraad, no; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade, yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad, no; Research Station—City, yes; Sardaukar—Emperor, no; Secrets—Bene Gesserit, no; Shipping—Spice Trade, no; Sietch Tabr—City, yes; Spice Refinery—City, yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad, no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists all 22 spaces, icons, and Combat labels.

answers.answer: A controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict when a Conflict card for that already-controlled location is revealed; it requires no Agent visit and is optional (‘may deploy’). After rewards, all players’ Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 defensive troop bonus; Critical Locations; Resolve Combat says all Combat markers reset to 0.

answers.answer: On an Agent turn, play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to a legal unoccupied space; resolve its Agent box and ignore its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard, nor move an Agent already on the board instead of sending one from your Leader; recall effects can return another Agent for a later turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one card from hand, send Agent from Leader, use Agent box; Recall Agent returns another Agent.

answers.answer: The restriction already applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent. He cannot postpone it by resolving board-space effects first; freedom to order effects does not delay the restriction.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications and FAQ Shaddam: restriction takes effect immediately on playing Signet Ring to send Agent.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths, first, second, and third places each receive their printed reward; fourth receives none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up, then checks for battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: in four players first, second and third can receive; highest strength wins and takes card.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: each player takes a Leader ‘choose, or select at random’.

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, not the Imperium Deck. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile; if the deck is empty, shuffle the discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards special rule.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup: shuffle House Hagal and place near Rival, retaining 2P Reshuffle.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. When acquired, a token moves from the bank onto that player’s garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: all four tokens in common bank, none assigned; later acquired token moves onto garrison.
